title.es: Subir lo que está en juego

es: Crear tensión en el inicio de una historia contrastando la rutina pasada (used to, would) con una ruptura en pasado simple y dejando claro lo que está en juego con un condicional.

vocabulary.es: estar en juego, pender de un hilo
mal presentimiento, nudo en el estómago

teaching.en: The stakes are what the character could lose, such as a job, a friendship or a home, and they must be named early so that the audience feels what is on the line.
teaching.es: Lo que está en juego es lo que el personaje podría perder, como un trabajo, una amistad o un hogar, y hay que nombrarlo pronto para que el público sienta lo que se arriesga.
teaching.explanationEs: Stakes es plural en este sentido: «the stakes are high»; on the line = en juego.
segments: The stakes are what the character could lose, such as a job, a friendship or a home,
and they must be named early so that the audience feels what is on the line.
teaching.audioText: The stakes are what the character could lose, such as a job, a friendship or a home, and they must be named early so that the audience feels what is on the line.

teaching.en: Back then we used to open at eight, and we would drink tea before the first customer arrived, in the quiet mornings that our routine had always given us.
teaching.es: Entonces solíamos abrir a las ocho y tomábamos té antes de que llegara el primer cliente, en las tranquilas mañanas que nuestra rutina siempre nos había dado.
teaching.explanationEs: Used to y would describen hábitos pasados; would solo con acciones, nunca con estados.
segments: Back then we used to open at eight, and we would drink tea before the
first customer arrived, in the quiet mornings that our routine had always given us.
teaching.audioText: Back then we used to open at eight, and we would drink tea before the first customer arrived, in the quiet mornings that our routine had always given us.

teaching.en: Then a letter arrived, and a threat began to loom over everything we had built, even though nobody said a word about it at dinner.
teaching.es: Entonces llegó una carta y una amenaza empezó a cernirse sobre todo lo que habíamos construido, aunque nadie dijo nada durante la cena.
teaching.explanationEs: Then + pasado simple marca la ruptura; threat es la amenaza; loom, que algo malo se acerca.
segments: Then a letter arrived, and a threat began to loom over everything we
had built, even though nobody said a word about it at dinner.
teaching.audioText: Then a letter arrived, and a threat began to loom over everything we had built, even though nobody said a word about it at dinner.

teaching.en: Without warning the risk became real: if we failed to pay by Friday, we would lose the shop, and the future of twelve families would hang in the balance.
teaching.es: Sin previo aviso el riesgo se volvió real: si no pagábamos el viernes, perderíamos la tienda y el futuro de doce familias estaría en juego.
teaching.explanationEs: If + pasado, would + verbo base, expresa el riesgo visto desde el pasado.
segments: Without warning the risk became real: if we failed to pay by Friday, we would
lose the shop, and the future of twelve families would hang in the balance.
teaching.audioText: Without warning the risk became real: if we failed to pay by Friday, we would lose the shop, and the future of twelve families would hang in the balance.

teaching.en: The call did not just disrupt our routine, it left me with a sinking feeling and a growing dread of the weekend.
teaching.es: La llamada no solo alteró nuestra rutina, me dejó con un mal presentimiento y un temor creciente por el fin de semana.
teaching.explanationEs: Disrupt es alterar algo que funcionaba; dread es un miedo que crece con la espera.
segments: The call did not just disrupt our routine, it left me
with a sinking feeling and a growing dread of the weekend.
teaching.audioText: The call did not just disrupt our routine, it left me with a sinking feeling and a growing dread of the weekend.

teaching.en: For years the routine had felt permanent and was simply taken for granted, which is exactly why the letter hit so hard.
teaching.es: Durante años la rutina había parecido permanente y se daba por hecho, y por eso la carta golpeó tan fuerte.
teaching.explanationEs: Taken for granted: algo que se da por seguro y no se valora hasta que está en peligro.
segments: For years the routine had felt permanent and was simply taken
for granted, which is exactly why the letter hit so hard.
teaching.audioText: For years the routine had felt permanent and was simply taken for granted, which is exactly why the letter hit so hard.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que describe una rutina pasada que ya terminó.

choices.text: We were opening the shop at eight when the phone rang.
We used to open the shop at eight and drink tea first.
We have opened the shop at eight every day since the beginning of spring.

feedback.es: «Used to» expresa un hábito pasado que ya no continúa; el pasado continuo es una acción interrumpida y el presente perfecto sigue vigente.

hint.es: Busca el hábito que ya no existe.

origin.text: The narrator is describing the quiet mornings before the trouble started, when nothing seemed likely to change in the little shop by the station.

prompt.es: Completa: «Cada domingo mi abuelo nos llevaba a pescar al río.»

feedback.es: Para una acción repetida en el pasado sirven would y used to.

hint.es: Hábito de acción: hay dos formas posibles.

origin.text: Every Sunday my grandfather ___ take us fishing on the river, and we never came home before dark. Then the doctor told him he had to rest.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Solíamos compartir un apartamento pequeño encima de la panadería.»

answer.text: We used to share a tiny flat above the bakery

feedback.es: «Used to» va seguido del verbo base: share.

hint.es: Empieza por el sujeto y «used to».

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué amenaza rompe la rutina y qué podría perderse.

choices.text: The river is flooding, and the villagers could lose all of their houses.
The mayor has resigned, and the village could lose its school.
The river is dirty, and the fishing families could lose their living.

feedback.es: La rutina (nadar y dormir junto al río) se rompe cuando el agua se vuelve negra, y lo que está en juego es el sustento de las familias que pescan y el lugar donde crecieron.

origin.audio: Every summer we would swim in the river, and we used to sleep outside near the water, even when the nights were cold. Nobody worried, because the river had always been clean. Then, one morning, the water turned black, and the smell hung over the whole village. The mayor said that a company further up the river was responsible. If it did not stop, the families who fished would lose their living, and we would lose the place where we had grown up.

prompt.es: Completa: «Éramos felices en esa casa, pero ahora está vacía.»

feedback.es: Be es un estado, por eso se usa used to y no would.

origin.text: The rooms are cold and empty now. We ___ be so happy in that house, but now the garden is full of weeds and nobody has opened the windows for years.

prompt.es: Elige la reescritura que añade lo que está en juego.

choices.text: My parents used to run a small bakery, and we would open at six. Then a man in a suit came, and if they refused to sign, they would lose the shop.
My parents used to run a small bakery, and we would open at six. Then a man in a suit came, and everybody in the kitchen felt very sad and worried about the future.
My parents ran a small bakery, and one morning a man in a suit came to see them, and he was very tall, friendly and kind to everyone in the shop.

feedback.es: Incluye rutina, ruptura y un riesgo concreto con «if… would»; las otras dos no dicen qué se puede perder.

origin.text: My parents ran a small bakery. One morning, a man in a suit came to see them.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué teme perder realmente la narradora.

choices.text: The fishing boat that her grandfather had kept for years.
Their shared mornings and her grandfather's sense of purpose.
Her place at school and the friends she had made.

feedback.es: Teme perder las mañanas juntos y, sobre todo, lo único que hacía sentirse vivo a su abuelo: lo que está en juego es emocional, no material.

origin.audio: My grandfather would wake me at five, and we used to fish until noon. Then the doctor said that he must not walk the river path again. I was afraid that I would lose our mornings together, and, worse, that he would lose the only thing that made him feel alive. For weeks I pretended that nothing had changed.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué revela «I pretended that nothing had changed».

choices.text: She had forgotten what the doctor had said about the river path.
She was angry with her grandfather for following the doctor's advice.
She was trying to keep the routine alive to protect them both.

feedback.es: Fingir que nada había cambiado es un modo de proteger la rutina y de evitar que el miedo se haga real para los dos.

origin.audio: My grandfather would wake me at five, and we used to fish until noon. Then the doctor said that he must not walk the river path again. I was afraid that I would lose our mornings together, and, worse, that he would lose the only thing that made him feel alive. For weeks I pretended that nothing had changed.

prompt.es: Completa: «Si el banco se negaba a otra prórroga, perderíamos la tienda.»

feedback.es: El riesgo se expresa con «if» + pasado simple en la condición y «would» + verbo base en la consecuencia; could o might también suavizan el riesgo.

origin.text: We had never missed a payment in twenty years. If the bank refused one more delay, we ___ lose the shop, and that was the risk we lived with every day of that winter.

prompt.es: Escribe un inicio de historia con rutina, amenaza y riesgo.

answer.text: My grandmother and I used to prepare the tickets every Friday before opening, and she would hum old songs while she worked. Then one day a letter arrived from the landlord, and a cold feeling settled over the little cinema. If we could not find the rent by Monday, we would lose the cinema, and with it her whole life.
accepted: My grandmother and I used to prepare the tickets every Friday before opening, and she would hum old songs while she worked. Then one day a letter arrived from the landlord, and a cold feeling settled over the little cinema. If we could not find the rent by Monday, we would lose the cinema, and with it her whole life.

In those days my grandmother and I would tidy the seats and count the tickets before the doors opened. One afternoon a letter came from the landlord. If we did not pay the rent by Monday, we would lose the cinema, and I could not stop thinking about it.

feedback.es: El inicio reúne rutina con used to o would, una ruptura en pasado simple y un riesgo con condicional.

origin.text: Datos: tu familia tenía un pequeño cine de barrio y cada viernes tu abuela y tú preparaban las entradas antes de abrir; un día llegó una carta del dueño del edificio; si no pagaban el alquiler antes del lunes, perderían el cine. Usa used to o would, pasado simple y un condicional.

prompt.es: Lee el borrador y elige la mejora que más tensión añadiría.

choices.text: A sentence naming what they could lose if they signed
A longer description of the porch and of the road
A paragraph about the man's job and where he lived

feedback.es: El borrador tiene rutina y ruptura pero no dice qué se arriesga: nombrar lo que perderían añade más tensión que más descripción.

origin.text: Every evening we would sit on the porch and watch the road, and that was our routine for twenty years. One day a man came with some papers. We were upset.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué convierte el anuncio en una amenaza real para los niños.

choices.text: It tells them that the town hall has changed its plans.
It names a concrete loss that touches their daily lives.
It explains that the new school is too far away.

feedback.es: La amenaza se vuelve real porque se dice exactamente qué se perdería: amigos, maestros y el único lugar seguro.

origin.audio: We used to play in the school yard every afternoon. Then the town hall announced that the school would close at the end of the year. If it closed, we would lose our friends, our teachers and the only place where we felt safe.

prompt.es: Completa: «La llamada no solo alteró nuestra rutina: llenó a la familia de temor.»

feedback.es: Disrupt es alterar algo que funcionaba con normalidad, como una rutina familiar.

origin.text: Nobody expected the news. The phone call did not simply ___ our routine; it filled the whole family with dread for the rest of the week.
